2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of his appeal, are that the appellant filed aforesaid with petition seeking declaration that the order dated 16.10.1993 staying the order of de-requisition dated 29.07.1993 communicated under Memo No. 331/L.A. dated 10.11.1993 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Feni and the order passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Feni communicated under Memo No. L.A.122(3) dated 23.03.1995 purportedly cancelling the order of de-requisition dated 29.07.1993 and initiation of proceeding under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (in short, the Act) in respect of the land measuring an area of 37.53 acres of Mouza Purbo Bijoy Singh as khas land and the notification No. 73 (16)/ Bhumi dated 30.07.1995 issued by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sadar, Feni are unlawful and have no legal effect. 

 3. In the writ petition, it was, inter alia, stated that Khaiz Ahmed and his five brothers purchased the property appertaining to C.S. khatian Nos. 2-7 and Plot No.1 of Mouza Purbo Bijoy Singh under Police Station Feni by 6 separate sale deeds executed and registered by Gyanotosh Roy Chowdhury. Khaiz Ahmed and his brothers, after purchase, got their names mutated in the khatian and paid rent. During S.A. operation, separate khatians were prepared in the names of Khaiz Ahmed and his brothers. By way of amicable partition, heirs of Khaiz Ahmed got 6.25 acres of land in their shares. The purchasers of "dighi", in question, undertook pisiculture project and having had seen the profit from the project many people became jealous. Feni Central Co-operative Bank made a proposal for requisition of the said "dighi" for the purpose of stating pisiculture project. The proposal of the Feni Central Co-operative Bank was rejected. Later on, Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali initiated Requision Case No. 49 of 1959-60 under the provision of (Emergency) Requisition of Project Act, 1948 for requisition of the land of said "Bijoy Singh Dighi" for the purpose of initiating pisiculture project by the Fisheries Directorate. The authority, thereafter, leased out the same to the local Christian Baptist Mission at a premium of tk. 10,000/- per annum. The said Mission, being totally unsuccessful in their project, surrendered the same to the Fisheries Directorate in 1982. The appellant No.2 went to the local tahshil office in 1990 to pay rent but the Tahasilder refused to accept the rent and, thereupon, the appellant No.2 preferred appeal and in appeal it was directed to the Tahasider to accept rent. The appellant No.2, on 01.10.1991, submitted a representation to the Deputy Commissioner, Feni for making de-requisition of the said "dighi" and to restore possession thereof. Thereupon, the Deputy Commissioner, by an order dated 29.07.1993, passed a direction for restoration of possession of the same to the appellant No.2. In the light of the decision for de-requisition, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Feni issued notice on 13.09.1993 to the persons from whom possession of the same was taken over upon requisition. The claimants of the "dighi" filed applications on 21.09.1993 marraring their claim and prayed for restoration of possession of the same. On the date fixed i.e. on 22.09.1993, appellant No.2 appeared before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and produced documents of title in support of their claim who being satisfied made recommendation for restoration of the possession of the disputed "dighi" to the owners. Thereupon, the matter was placed before the Deputy Commissioner but the Deputy Commissioner stayed the operation of the decision of de-requisition by his order dated 16.10.1993 and, ultimately, upon raising question of including the property in the khas khatian No.1 by his order dated 31.12.1993. The Deputy Commissioner, Feni issued a letter addressing the office of Commissioner, Chittagong Division, seeking direction for the disposal of the matter and the Divisional Commissioner, Feni that he is legally authorized to decide the matter and directed him to dispose of the matter. Thereafter, the Deputy Commissioner, Feni passed and order dated 23.03.1995 to the effect that the S.A. recorded tenants have failed to prove their title and ownership of the disputed "dighi" and, accordingly, started proceeding under section 92 of the Act for making the property khas. Thereafter, the Assistant Commissioner, (Land), Feni issued notice dated 30.07.1995 under section 92(3) of the Act stating, that he would take over possession of the same on 31.08.1995. It was the contention of the writ petitioners that the Deputy Commissioner had no lawful authority to pass order staying de-requisition and, thereafter, to cancel the order of de-requisition and further to make any order under the provision of Section 92 of the Act for listing the "dighi", in question, in khas khatian and that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) illegally issued the notice dated 30.07.1995 under Section 92(3) of the Act. It was further contended that the appellants are entitled to get restoration of possession of the "dight" in view of the provision of section 8 of the (emergency) Repulsion of Property Act, 1998 and the Rules framed there under. The action of the respondents in respect of the "dighi", in question, is arbitrary and without lawful authority and suffers from procedural impropriety and the action of the respondents infringes the fundamental rights of the appellants as guaranteed by articles 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution. 

 6. Mr. Md. Zafarullah Chowdhury, learned Counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the High Court Division erred in law in deciding the question of title holding that the appellants heave no title in the disputed property. He submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in holding that he property, in question, stood acquired by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act inasmuch as there was no material on record to support the finding that the interest of Gyonotosh Ray Chowdhury in the said property stood acquired under the said Act. He further submits that the Government has requisitioned the property, in question, upon issuing notice to the predecessor-in-interest of the appellants. Therefore, the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that the Government is stopped from claiming the property as khas land. He further submits that the High Court Division misread the gazette notification issued under section 3 of the Stated Acquisition and Tenancy Act and came to a wrong finding that the interest of Gaynotosh Roy Chowdhury was acquired in 1954. 

 (2) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6) of section 20, the Government may also, simultaneously with or at any time after the publication of a notification under sub-section (1) in respect of the interest of any rent-receiver in any estate, taluk, tenure, holding or tenancy, acquire, by notification in the official Gazette, with effect from such date as may be specified in the notification (hereinafter referred to as the notified date), all or any of the lands in his hkas possession of which he shall he shall not be entitled to retain possession under the said section and so much of the lands in his khas possession as has been acquired under this sub-section and has not vested in the Government under clause (a) of the sub-section (4), shall vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances.------” 

 15. Since the title of the property in question, vested in the Government free from all encumbrances in 1954, the subsequent acts of the Government, that is, requisition of the property and, lastly, steps of making the said property khas under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act are redundant.
